chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Hisham ibn Salim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man wakes up not intending to fast, and when the day rises, a thought comes to him about fasting. He said: 'If he intends fasting before the sun passes its zenith (Zawal), his day is counted for him; and if he intends it after Zawal, only the time from which he intended is counted for him.'

key_terms.زَوَال: The passing of the sun from its zenith (midday)
key_terms.يَوْمُهُ: His day (the full day of fasting)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting if one intends to fast after midday?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the flexibility of intention (niyyah) for voluntary or make-up fasting, distinguishing between pre-midday and post-midday decisions. It establishes that while early intention validates the full day, late intention only counts from the moment of resolve, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the validity of the fast is tied to the duration of conscious commitment. This ruling is foundational in the chapter of Fasting within *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, illustrating the practical application of intention in daily worship.
